description: The bar chart visually represents the distribution of morphosyntactic probing tasks across ten linguistic families, with categories listed along the vertical axis in descending order of task count: IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque. Each category is represented by a distinct colored horizontal bar extending along the horizontal axis, labeled “# tasks,” which spans from 0 to 80 in increments of 10. IE-Slavic, shown in light blue, has the longest bar, reaching approximately 80 tasks. IE-Romance (dark blue) follows with about 48 tasks, while IE-Germanic (light green) and Uralic (green) are both near 45 tasks. IE-Baltic (pink) drops sharply to around 18 tasks, and IE-other (red) is slightly lower at about 16. IE-Indic (beige) and Semitic (orange) are both near 10 tasks, Turkic (lavender) is at approximately 6, and Basque (purple) is the shortest at roughly 4 tasks. The chart visually emphasizes a steep decline from IE-Slavic to IE-Baltic, followed by a more gradual tapering among the remaining families, highlighting the disproportionate focus on Indo-European branches—particularly Slavic—in multilingual BERT probing studies.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of tasks across various linguistic families. The vertical axis lists the categories, including IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, arranged in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis is labeled '# tasks,' ranging from 0 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 10. IE-Slavic exhibits the highest number of tasks, approximately 80, followed by IE-Romance at around 60 tasks. IE-Germanic and Uralic show similar task counts, both exceeding 40 tasks. Notably, IE-Baltic demonstrates a sharp decline compared to Uralic, with fewer than 15 tasks. Basque, the smallest category, has fewer than 10 tasks, showing a consistent trend of minimal representation across studies. The chart highlights a steady decrease in task counts from IE-Slavic to IE-Baltic, with a more gradual decline observed among the remaining categories.
